title: A/B testing metrics cardinality review (route-level experiments) — checklist + limits
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- We’re adding route-level A/B testing. This introduces new metric dimensions (experiment_id, variant, etc.) that can easily blow up series count if we’re not strict.
- Goal: define an allowlisted tag set + limits and an instrumentation plan (metrics + exposure events) that supports Console reporting and guardrails without melting metrics storage.
- Scope here is metrics/traces/logging for the v1 beta and GA criteria for “safe to enable broadly”.

Assumptions (call these out so we can sanity-check)
- Traffic volume: large customers can do 10^3–10^5 RPS aggregated across projects.
- # concurrent experiments per org: usually small (1–10), but we must assume worst-case “someone creates a lot”.
- We need breakdowns by variant for latency + errors + cost; we do NOT need arbitrary per-user breakdowns.
- Experiment results in Console should come primarily from aggregated datasets/jobs (not ad-hoc PromQL over every label permutation).

Non-goals for observability v1
- No per-prompt/per-request “debug dimensions” on metrics (those belong in sampled logs/traces).
- No free-form customer tags piped into Redwood metrics.
- No dimension that can vary per request (request_id, prompt_hash, raw route path, api_key) on metrics.

Terminology (to reduce cross-team confusion)
- exposure event: a structured event emitted once per request that records which experiment + variant was assigned (used for experiment analytics and joins).
- guardrail metrics: low-latency aggregated metrics used for alerting/auto-rollback (TTFT/latency/error thresholds).
- reporting datasets: post-processed aggregates powering Console experiment results.

Where we’ve seen cardinality explosions historically (lessons learned)
- Labeling metrics by raw HTTP path (e.g., /v1/chat/completions?project_id=…) or customer-supplied route names.
- Tagging with model_version including build metadata (every deploy creates “new model”).
- Propagating request headers into tags (x-user-id, x-session-id, trace_id).
- Unbounded error dimensions (full exception string, upstream error message).

Proposed tag allowlist (v1)

A) Global approach
- Metrics emitted in the gateway/runtime MUST use an explicit allowlist for labels.
- Any non-allowlisted label should be dropped at source (not “maybe filtered later”).
- Use normalized identifiers:
  - route_id: internal stable route template id (not literal path). Example: “route_2f9a3c” computed at config time.
  - experiment_id: stable UUID-ish id; do not include human name.
  - variant_id: small (A/B/…) stable id; do not include full model name.
  - model_family: small set (e.g., llama3, mistral, qwen) if needed; avoid model_version.
  - region: limited set of cloud regions.

B) Explicit allowlist for experiment metrics
Allowed labels (recommended max values in parentheses)
- experiment_id (<= 200 active globally per region; see limits below)
- variant_id (<= 8)
- route_id (<= 5k globally; but per experiment we expect <= 10)
- project_id (optional; for internal-only debugging, NOT for customer dashboards; see below)
- region (<= 30)
- outcome (success|error|timeout|rate_limited) (<= 4)
- http_status_class (2xx|4xx|5xx) (<= 3)
- error_category (small enum; <= 20)
- deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated) (<= 2)
- is_streaming (true|false) (<= 2)

Disallowed labels (hard NO)
- tenant_id / org_id (too many; use experiment_id + route_id; tenants can query via datasets)
- api_key_id
- user_id / end_user_id
- request_id / trace_id / span_id
- raw path / raw host / raw URL
- prompt_hash / prompt_id / eval_prompt_id (belongs in eval pipeline, not prod metrics)
- model_version / model_sha / build_id
- error_message / exception_class if unbounded
- any customer-provided header value

Recommended compromise for project/org scoping
- For alerting + dashboards, do NOT include org_id/project_id as metric labels.
- Instead:
  - guardrails alert on experiment_id + variant_id + route_id + region.
  - Console drilldowns use reporting datasets keyed by experiment_id (joins to org/project happen in the analytics store with access controls).
- If we absolutely need “project scope” in metrics for internal debugging, make it:
  - behind an internal-only feature flag
  - sampled (e.g., 1%)
  - emitted as logs/events, not as metric labels.

Cardinality budget (numbers we can use to evaluate PRs)

Budget target (per region)
- Incremental series introduced by A/B testing should stay < 250k time series / region.
  - Rationale: we’re already tight in eu-west; adding A/B must not double baseline.

Rough upper bound math (guardrail metrics)
- Suppose:
  - active experiments in region: E
  - variants per experiment: V
  - routes per experiment: R
  - outcomes: O
  - streaming: S
  - status_class: H
  - error_category (only for failures): C
- For a single counter metric keyed by (experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region, outcome, is_streaming):
  - series ~= E * V * R * O * S
- If E=50, V=2, R=3, O=4, S=2 => 50*2*3*4*2 = 2,400 series for that metric. That’s OK.
- The risk comes from adding route_id at “global” scale (5k+) or adding project/org labels.

Where it gets dangerous
- If we label by raw route path and customers create per-tenant routes, R can blow up quickly.
- If we label by project_id and we have P=10k active projects, multiplying everything by 10k makes any metric unusable.

Therefore the policy is:
- route_id must be normalized, stable, and bounded.
- do not label by project/org on metrics.
- experiment_id count must be bounded (limits + TTL cleanup).

Hard limits / guardrails we should implement (source-side, not “best effort”)

1) Active experiment cap
- Control plane should enforce a per-project cap on concurrently RUNNING experiments affecting the same route.
  - Proposed: max 3 running experiments per project total; max 1 per route_id.
  - (Overlapping rollouts are already tricky; this also protects cardinality.)

2) Variant cap per experiment
- Proposed max variants per experiment: 8 (UI can still call it “A/B” but backend generic).

3) Route selector constraints
- Experiment config must target a route_id (template) not arbitrary glob of routes.
- “All routes in project” is disallowed for v1.

4) Label allowlist enforcement in gateway
- Emit metrics through an internal helper that takes a typed struct; do not allow ad-hoc tag maps.
- Enforce:
  - label key allowlist
  - label value validation (length cap, charset cap)
  - “unknown enum” -> mapped to “other” bucket

5) Error categorization
- error_category must be a stable enum defined in code.
- If upstream gives a new error, map to “other_upstream_error” until explicitly added.
- Never include free-form error messages.

6) Retention / rollup strategy
- High-resolution (per-minute) series retention: 14 days.
- Downsample/rollup for 90 days (or move to analytics store for Console reporting).
- Experiments older than 90 days: results only via exported report artifacts / analytics (not via raw metrics queries).

Metric inventory (what we plan to emit)

A) Must-have for guardrails + quick diagnosis
1) Request count
- Name: rw_ab_request_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region, deployment_mode, is_streaming

2) Error count
- Name: rw_ab_request_error_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region, deployment_mode, is_streaming, outcome, http_status_class, error_category
- Notes:
  - outcome should be derived consistently across gateway/runtime.

3) End-to-end latency
- Name: rw_ab_request_latency_ms
- Type: histogram
- Labels: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region, deployment_mode, is_streaming

4) Time to first token (TTFT) (streaming)
- Name: rw_ab_ttft_ms
- Type: histogram
- Labels: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region, deployment_mode
- Notes:
  - Only emit when streaming=true; don’t add streaming label if it makes queries harder; decide one approach and stick to it.

5) Tokens
- Name: rw_ab_tokens_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region, deployment_mode, token_type (prompt|completion)

6) Cost attribution (metering derived)
- Name: rw_ab_cost_usd_total (or cost_microdollars_total)
- Type: counter
- Labels: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region, deployment_mode
- Notes:
  - This should use the same cost attribution path as billing; do not create a second “approx cost” pipeline for experiments.

B) Nice-to-have (explicitly gated to avoid series explosion)
- queue_delay_ms histogram by experiment_id/variant_id ONLY (no route_id) if we need to separate “routing/queueing” from “model compute”.

Exposure event design (how it relates to cardinality)
- Exposure events can carry more dimensions because they live in a log/event pipeline, not Prometheus-style time series.
- Still need cardinality discipline because BigQuery/Snowflake costs and query times scale with width and distinct values.

Exposure event: recommended fields (high level)
- required identifiers: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id
- request context: timestamp, region, deployment_mode, is_streaming
- join keys (privacy-safe): project_id (OK here), org_id (OK here), but NOT end_user_id unless explicitly provided as a salted hash and approved in ADR-0188.
- latency/cost fields: numeric values can live in the event to power aggregates without metric joins.

Sampling policy
- Metrics (guardrails): no sampling.
- Exposure events: sample at a configurable rate (default 1.0 for beta partners with low volume; default 0.1 for GA). Provide per-project override with an upper bound.
- IMPORTANT: If sampling exposure events, the Console must be sampling-aware (estimation + confidence intervals) and clearly label it.

Checklist for PR reviews (copy/paste into GitHub reviews)

Labeling checklist
[ ] Are all metric labels on the approved allowlist?
[ ] Is any label derived from request headers? (If yes -> block.)
[ ] Is route labeled by route_id/template id (NOT raw path)?
[ ] Is model labeled by model_family (or omitted) rather than full model_version?
[ ] Are error labels bounded (enum) and mapped to “other”?
[ ] Are label values length-capped and charset-validated?

Cardinality estimation checklist
[ ] Have we estimated worst-case series count per region for the new metric?
[ ] Does this metric multiply by route_id + experiment_id + region at the same time?
[ ] Does the metric add project_id/org_id as a label? (If yes -> block or gate.)
[ ] Is the metric a histogram? If yes, remember histogram series multiply by bucket count.

Operational checklist
[ ] Is there a feature flag to disable experiment metric emission quickly?
[ ] Are there dashboards/alerts to detect cardinality increases (ingestion rate, series count)?
[ ] Is there a runbook link for rollback if we hit cardinality limits?

Proposed automated protections

1) Build-time linting
- Add a lint check in gateway/runtime code: “experiment metrics must be emitted through ExperimentMetrics helper”.
- Helper only exposes the allowlisted labels.

2) Runtime safeguards
- If experiment_id is missing/invalid, do not emit experiment metrics (emit baseline route metrics only).
- If route_id missing, map route_id="unknown" (bounded) rather than using raw path.
- If experiment_id cardinality exceeds threshold in-process (LRU estimate), log a high-severity warning and drop experiment_id label (fallback to “experiment_id=overflow”).
  - Note: This is a last-resort safety valve; primary protection should be config limits.

3) Monitoring for series spikes
- Add internal dashboard panels:
  - total active time series per cluster
  - top-N label values by series count (experiment_id, route_id)
  - ingestion rate (samples/sec) before/after enabling A/B
- Alert: “ab_testing_metrics_series_count_delta > X% over 30m” routes to #eng-sre + oncall.

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Do we include route_id on all A/B metrics or only on a subset?
- Pro: route-level diagnosis
- Con: multipliers for series
- Proposal: include route_id on latency/error/request count; omit it on cost if cost is already aggregated by experiment/variant (unless needed).

2) Do we include is_streaming as a label or split metrics by name?
- Label keeps names short but increases label permutations.
- Split-by-name reduces label cardinality but creates more metric names.
- Proposal: keep is_streaming only where necessary; for TTFT, metric implies streaming.

3) Region dimension
- For guardrails we need region.
- For Console results, aggregation can happen across regions; but the dataset can preserve region for drilldowns.

4) Dedicated deployments
- Dedicated may have many isolated clusters. Does this increase region-like dimension count?
- Proposal: do not label by cluster_id. Keep deployment_mode + region, and for dedicated cluster-level debugging use traces/logs.

Action items (owners / due dates)
- [Allison Grant] Add “Experiment metric label allowlist” section to Confluence observability standard. Due 2026-02-23.
- [Caleb Johnson] Implement gateway-side allowlist enforcement + value validation helper. Tie to PR_18415 follow-up. Due 2026-02-26.
- [Logan Wright] Confirm exposure event sampling defaults and Console sampling-aware messaging. Due 2026-02-25.
- [Nadia Rahman] Validate cost metric tags align with billing attribution (no new dimensions). Due 2026-02-27.
- [Aisha Bello] Add series-count monitoring + alert in observability-pack. Due 2026-02-28.

Appendix: Proposed error_category enum (draft)
- upstream_timeout
- upstream_429
- upstream_5xx
- gateway_timeout
- gateway_rate_limited
- validation_error
- auth_error
- capacity_unavailable
- streaming_disconnect
- internal_error
- other

Appendix: “Route id” definition
- route_id is computed from the configured API route template and project context at config time.
- Examples:
  - /v1/chat/completions (template) => route_id=route_2f9a3c
  - /v1/embeddings => route_id=route_b19c11
- Do not include query params.
- Do not include project_id in the route_id.

Notes / references
- See ADR-0188 for privacy rules (especially for exposure logs).
- See PR_18519 for the tag reduction proposal; this doc should be consistent with final implementation.
- For rollback guidance, see runbook: confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/ab-testing-emergency-disable-and-rollback (link in artifacts).
